mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved monotonically across all four snapshot weeks (-74.3 to -66.9), and this transit-commuting recovery mechanically replenishes pedestrian flow into retail corridors, so RETAIL_REC continues rising over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved every week from -74.3 at t-3w to -66.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days while TRANSIT continues its four-week monotone improvement.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen from 23.3 to 19.4, meaning household time at home is shrinking; each point of residential outflow releases discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks in proportion to the residential decline.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1.5 points below its t-3w level
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 23.3 -> 19.4 over the four snapshot weeks
regime_hint: gradual reopening with stay-at-home guidance lifting
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops at least 1.5 points below its t-3w level and the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is still at or below the prior-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS (-43.7 to -29.6) and WORKPLACES (-64.0 to -54.1) are rising jointly, and their co-movement identifies a genuine out-of-home normalization rather than a single-category artifact; the joint signal lifts RETAIL_REC over two weeks more than either series alone would.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 14.1 points and WORKPLACES rose 9.9 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where both PARKS and WORKPLACES are above their t-3w levels, the subsequent 28-day RETAIL_REC mean fails to exceed the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM improving from -39.1 to -32.0 under partial restrictions shows essential-errand caps loosening ahead of discretionary re-openings; because grocery relaxations historically precede retail-and-recreation relaxations by two to four weeks, RETAIL_REC rises with a policy-lag.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 7.1 points from t-3w to t-0w
regime_hint: phased reopening with capacity limits still binding on retail
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM improves for four consecutive weeks while the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean stays at or below the trailing-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The 14-point PARKS recovery to -29.6 represents outdoor substitution: households reallocate released discretionary time and budget to parks rather than indoor retail, so RETAIL_REC over the next week is pulled down relative to its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points above its t-3w level
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS gained 14.1 points from t-3w to t-0w, the largest recovery of any category
regime_hint: warm-weather reopening with parks capacity unrestricted
failure_condition: PARKS rises more than 10 points above its t-3w level and RETAIL_REC in the following week is higher than its trailing four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing the -70 level marks the point at which discretionary transit trips (not just essential commuting) return; once crossed, retail footfall accelerates, so a TRANSIT reading above -70 predicts higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -70 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT broke above -70 at t-1w (-69.9) and held at t-0w (-66.9)
failure_condition: On weeks where TRANSIT is above -70, the next-14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the trailing-14-day mean in the majority of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS crossing above -30 signals the seasonal outdoor-activity peak, and the associated warm-weather discretionary travel habit spills into retail-and-recreation trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks on a seasonal rather than policy clock.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above -30 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached -29.6 at t-0w, its highest reading in the snapshot
failure_condition: PARKS stays above -30 for the next four weeks while the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean is at or below the trailing-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remains elevated near 19-23 points above baseline, so home-centered consumption persists and caps the retail rebound; as long as RESIDENTIAL stays above 18, RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks stays below its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 18 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has stayed above 19 in every snapshot week despite steady decline
regime_hint: home-confinement steady state with voluntary distancing
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains above 18 for the next four weeks while the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the trailing-28-day mean.
